label: Employees (owner included)
note: Everyone on payroll. No contractors: hours beyond capacity are simply not available.

label: Cost per employee, fully loaded
note: Salary, payroll tax and benefits. One blended rate for designers, estimators and craftspeople.

label: Overhead per employee
note: Floor space, tools, software seats and insurance that grow with headcount.

label: Productive hours per employee per year
note: Hours actually spent on quoting, design, forming and handling.

label: Coordination loss per additional coworker
note: Each extra person costs everyone this share of their hours in meetings and handoffs. The organizational source of diseconomies of scale.

label: Fixed overhead (annual)
note: Accounting, legal, general liability, office. Does not grow with headcount.

label: Cost of capital
note: Charged on per-design outlays from order until the customer pays.

label: Customer payment terms after delivery
note: Net-30 to net-60 plus retainage is normal in construction.

label: Price per panel
note: 4 x 10 ft doubly curved aluminum panel, supplied not installed. About $2,080/m² ($193/ft²).

label: Units per design (batch size)
note: How many identical panels share one geometry. Freeform facades often run 1 to 6.

label: Marketing cost per qualified lead
note: Bid boards, trade shows, sample panels, per architect or contractor who asks for a quote.

label: Win rate if delivery were instant
note: Share of quotes that become orders before lead time is considered.

label: Lead time that halves the win rate
note: Construction schedules punish slow suppliers.

label: Local market depth (leads/yr before lead cost doubles)
note: Custom facade work is regional and thin. The demand-side source of rising marginal cost.

label: Market saturation curvature
note: How sharply lead cost climbs past market depth.

label: Base marketing (annual)
note: Website, portfolio photography, AIA and CSI memberships.

label: Chance the architect revises after tooling is made
note: A die absorbs a revision badly, a buck moderately, a toolpath cheaply.

label: Hours per unit: handling, QC, install coordination
Design hours per geometry
note: Geometry must be made die-formable: draw depth, addendum, springback.

label: Design hours per geometry
note: Buck model plus a forming plan for the craftspeople.

label: Design hours per geometry
note: CAD goes straight to toolpath with fewer formability constraints.

label: Aluminum in the finished panel
note: 3.6 m² of 3 mm 5052 ≈ 29 kg at about $7/kg delivered.

label: Coating and packing per panel
note: PVDF paint or anodize. Same for every route.

label: Material utilization
note: Binder and addendum trimmed after the draw.

label: Material utilization
note: Near-net blanks, trimmed by hand.

label: Material utilization
note: The clamping frame border is scrap.

label: Draw die per geometry
note: Large 4 x 10 ft draw die. Soft zinc-alloy or epoxy $20k–60k; hardened steel $100k+.

label: Die design engineering
note: Often left out of the die quote.

label: Die rework when the design changes
note: Share of die cost.

label: Press host rate
note: Large-bed press, per hour.

label: CNC-milled buck per geometry
note: MDF or foam form the craftspeople shape the panel against.

label: Forming hours per panel
note: English wheel, stretching, planishing, weld repair. Coachbuilders spend 40–100+ hours on a hood-sized panel.

label: Rework or scrap rate
note: Panels that miss the ±2 mm joint tolerance and are remade.

label: Trim and edge prep per panel
Forming shop (annual)
note: Wheels, power hammer, welders, extra floor space.

label: Programming and first article per geometry
note: Toolpath, frame setup, first-part scan. Synthetic: Machina publishes no pricing.

label: Robot hours per panel (form, scan, trim)
Cell rate per robot-hour
note: Including Machina's margin. Synthetic.

label: Surface finishing per panel
note: Stated finish is 125 µin Ra, so visible faces are blended before coating.

label: Miles: Machina factory to site
note: Worst case: the Los Angeles factory. Best case: a regional factory that does not exist yet.

label: Lead time
note: Die design, build, tryout and run.

label: Lead time
note: Machina: first parts typically within a week of CAD. Worst case adds cross-country freight.

label: Supplier coordination hours per geometry
note: Remote reviews and time-zone delay versus a short drive.
